meta.title: The 3 Questions Every Soul Is Asked in the Grave
meta.description:
What are the 3 questions in the grave? The Prophet ﷺ told us exactly what Munkar and Nakir ask
every soul after burial, and what the believer answers. Every hadith here is authentic and sourced below.

Chapters
0:00 The 3 questions
0:30 The footsteps
1:15 Munkar and Nakir
2:00 At the grave with the Prophet ﷺ
2:45 Question 1
4:00 Question 2
4:45 Question 3
5:40 "My servant has spoken the truth"
6:25 The one who fails
7:30 The barrier
8:05 The verse about the grave
8:50 The du'a the Prophet ﷺ used to make
9:30 The answers

Sources
Sahih al-Bukhari 1338, 1374, 1369 and 1377: https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1338
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1071 (Hasan): https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:1071
Sunan Abi Dawud 4753 (Sahih, Al-Albani): https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4753
Quran 14:27 and 23:99-100 (The Clear Quran, Dr. Mustafa Khattab): https://quran.com

Visuals are AI-assisted illustrations. The Prophet ﷺ and the angels are never shown with faces.

scenes.visual: Slow push-in on a quiet graveyard at dusk. Fresh soil on one grave. A lantern flickers.
scenes.prompt: Slow push-in on a quiet graveyard at dusk. Fresh soil on one grave. A lantern flickers.
scenes.vo: Before you die, you can know the 3 questions of the grave. Most people never learn them until it is too late.

scenes.visual: Text: "3 QUESTIONS". Wind sound.
scenes.prompt: Text: "3 QUESTIONS". Wind sound.
scenes.vo: And the Prophet ﷺ told us exactly what they are.

scenes.visual: Three glowing cards, face down, numbered 1 2 3.
scenes.prompt: Three glowing cards, face down, numbered 1 2 3.
scenes.vo: In the next few minutes, I'll take you through what happens in the grave, step by step, using only authentic hadith and the Quran. And by the end, you'll know the 3 questions, and the answers.

scenes.visual: Low angle from the grave: silhouettes of mourners walking away. Footsteps on gravel, fading.
scenes.prompt: Low angle from the grave: silhouettes of mourners walking away. Footsteps on gravel, fading.
scenes.vo: Imagine the burial is over. Your family says the last du'a, turns around, and starts walking away. The Prophet ﷺ said that the person in the grave hears them. He hears their footsteps leaving.

scenes.visual: Two tall shapes of white light appear in the darkness. No faces.
scenes.prompt: Two tall shapes of white light appear in the darkness. No faces.
scenes.vo: And it's in that moment, while their footsteps are still fading, that two angels come to him.

scenes.visual: Arabic calligraphy: منكر و نكير, glowing.
scenes.prompt: Arabic calligraphy: منكر و نكير, glowing.
scenes.vo: In a hadith in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ named them. Munkar. And Nakir.

scenes.visual: Inside a dim grave, a shrouded figure rising to sit, lit from above.
scenes.prompt: Inside a dim grave, a shrouded figure rising to sit, lit from above.
scenes.vo: In Sahih al-Bukhari, he described that they sit the person up. No more sleep. No more waiting. The questioning begins.

scenes.beat: BEAT 3. THE SETTING OF THE HADITH
scenes.visual: Wide shot, desert cemetery, companions seated around a figure whose face is covered by soft white light.
scenes.prompt: Wide shot, desert cemetery, companions seated around a figure whose face is covered by soft white light. Any Prophet or Companion is shown only as a robed figure whose entire face is covered by a soft glowing white light; no facial features visible.
scenes.vo: The fullest description comes from the companion al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him. He said they were at a funeral with the Prophet ﷺ, and he sat down at the grave. And before he told them anything, he asked Allah for protection from the punishment of the grave. Think about that. The Prophet ﷺ himself was asking for protection. So what is it that he was so careful about?
cards: Sunan Abi Dawud 4753, graded Sahih by Al-Albani

scenes.visual: First card flips: "1. Who is your Lord?"
scenes.prompt: First card flips: "1. Who is your Lord?"
scenes.vo: The first question: Who is your Lord? The believer answers: My Lord is Allah.

scenes.visual: Quick montage: a man skipping prayer, scrolling at night; then a man standing for Fajr.
scenes.prompt: Quick montage: a man skipping prayer, scrolling at night; then a man standing for Fajr.
scenes.vo: It sounds easy. Everyone in this video knows the answer right now. But this isn't a question you answer with your memory. It's a question you answer with your life.

scenes.visual: A lone figure in a dark room, phone light on his face turned away, a prayer mat rolled up in the corner.
scenes.prompt: A lone figure in a dark room, phone light on his face turned away, a prayer mat rolled up in the corner.
scenes.vo: Think about what "my Lord" really means. The one you obey when nobody is watching. The one you turn to when you're afraid. The one whose pleasure you chase, or whose anger you ignore.

scenes.visual: Pages of a diary turning by themselves in the wind, words fading.
scenes.prompt: Pages of a diary turning by themselves in the wind, words fading.
scenes.vo: For some people, the honest answer to "who is your Lord" would be their money. Their phone. What people think of them. In the grave, there is no time to think about it. The answer that comes out is the one your life already wrote.

scenes.visual: Second card flips: "2. What is your religion?"
scenes.prompt: Second card flips: "2. What is your religion?"
scenes.vo: The second: What is your religion? The believer says: My religion is Islam.

scenes.visual: Hands placing a coin in a charity box at night, a lantern beside it.
scenes.prompt: Hands placing a coin in a charity box at night, a lantern beside it.
scenes.vo: Not the religion written on your ID card. Not the religion of your family name. Islam means submission to Allah. So the question is really: did you submit? Did your prayers, your money, your words, your choices belong to Allah?

scenes.visual: Third card flips: "3. Who is this man who was sent among you?"
scenes.prompt: Third card flips: "3. Who is this man who was sent among you?"
scenes.vo: And the third: Who is this man who was sent among you? The believer says: He is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
scenes.card_text: 3. Who is this man who was sent among you?

scenes.visual: An old book of hadith open on a wooden stand, candlelight, pages gently lifting.
scenes.prompt: An old book of hadith open on a wooden stand, candlelight, pages gently lifting.
scenes.vo: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the believer says: I testify that he is Allah's slave and His Messenger. Notice: the angels don't ask "did you know his name?" Everyone knows his name. The believer answers because he followed him. He knew his sunnah, he loved him, he sent salawat upon him. You can't testify for someone you never got to know.

scenes.beat: BEAT 7. "MY SERVANT HAS SPOKEN THE TRUTH"
scenes.visual: Light pours down into the grave from above. Silence, then a single soft tone.
scenes.prompt: Light pours down into the grave from above. Silence, then a single soft tone.
scenes.vo: And then, in the narration of al-Bara', a caller calls out from the heavens: "My servant has spoken the truth."

scenes.beat: BEAT 7. "MY SERVANT HAS SPOKEN THE TRUTH"
scenes.visual: The walls of the grave move outward. Light fills the space.
scenes.prompt: The walls of the grave move outward. Light fills the space.
scenes.vo: And in the hadith of Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ said his grave is widened seventy cubits by seventy cubits.

scenes.visual: Light cuts out. Darkness. Heartbeat.
scenes.prompt: Light cuts out. Darkness. Heartbeat.
scenes.vo: But not everyone answers.

scenes.visual: A crowd of grey silhouettes all mouthing the same words; one figure among them, lost.
scenes.prompt: A crowd of grey silhouettes all mouthing the same words; one figure among them, lost.
scenes.vo: The disbeliever is asked the same questions. And he says: "Alas, alas. I do not know." In Sahih al-Bukhari, the hypocrite says: "I do not know. I used to say what the people used to say."

scenes.visual: Grave walls closing in, dust falling. No gore.
scenes.prompt: Grave walls closing in, dust falling. No gore.
scenes.vo: That line should scare every one of us. "I used to say what the people said." He went along with everyone. He never made the answer his own. He said the words, maybe even every Friday. But they were never his. The Prophet ﷺ said he is struck with an iron hammer, and in the hadith of Tirmidhi, the earth closes in on him.

scenes.visual: A hand reaching up through mist toward a closed gate of light.
scenes.prompt: A hand reaching up through mist toward a closed gate of light.
scenes.vo: And there is no going back. Allah tells us in the Quran that when death comes, a person cries out: "My Lord! Let me go back, so I may do good in what I left behind." And the answer is no. Behind them is a barrier, a barzakh, until the Day they are raised.

scenes.beat: BEAT 10. THE VERSE ABOUT THE GRAVE
scenes.visual: Calm night sky over the desert, one bright star, the verse reference in gold.
scenes.prompt: Calm night sky over the desert, one bright star, the verse reference in gold.
scenes.vo: So how does anyone pass? Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, the same companion, narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that this verse was revealed about the grave: "Allah makes the believers steadfast with the firm Word of faith in this worldly life and the Hereafter." Steadfast. Firm. The answers aren't something you cram for at the last moment. Allah makes them firm for the people who held on to them in this life. The same word, in this world and in the grave.

scenes.beat: BEAT 11. THE DU'A HE USED TO MAKE
scenes.visual: Text: "Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabil-qabr"
scenes.prompt: Text: "Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabil-qabr"
scenes.vo: And the Prophet ﷺ gave us one more thing. Abu Hurairah narrated, in Sahih al-Bukhari, that the Prophet ﷺ used to make this du'a: "O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the punishment of the grave, and from the punishment of the Fire, and from the trial of life and death, and from the trial of the Masih ad-Dajjal." If the Prophet ﷺ himself asked for this protection, how much more do we need it? Learn it tonight. Say it in your prayer.

scenes.visual: All three cards side by side.
scenes.prompt: All three cards side by side.
scenes.vo: So here they are. The 3 questions: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is this man who was sent among you? Now you know them. Before your death, not after. And now you know the verse, and the du'a.

scenes.visual: Back at the graveyard at dawn. The lantern still burning. Fajr adhan begins faintly.
scenes.prompt: Back at the graveyard at dawn. The lantern still burning. Fajr adhan begins faintly.
scenes.vo: The answers in the grave aren't memorised. They are lived. So the real question isn't "do you know the answers?" It's "will your life say them for you?"

scenes.visual: End screen with next video.
scenes.prompt: End screen with next video.
scenes.vo: Next, watch what the Quran says happens in Barzakh, the world between death and the Day of Judgment.
